question: A alone can finish a task in 20 days, while B alone can finish it in 15 days. They together work for 5 days and stop, then the rest of the work is finished by C alone in 2 days. If they get paid 2,400 for finishing the whole task, then find the difference between the daily wages of C and A.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(20, 15) = 60 units. Efficiency of **A** = 3, **B** = 4.

Work done by (A + B) in 5 days = (3 + 4) × 5 = 35 units.

Remaining work done by **C** = 60 − 35 = 25 units. Efficiency of **C** = 25 ÷ 2 = 12.5 units/day.

Total wage ₹ 2400 for 60 units ⇒ 1 unit = ₹ 40.

Difference in **daily wages** of **C** and **A** = (12.5 − 3) × 40 = 9.5 × 40 = ₹ 380.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **A** alone takes 20 days, **B** alone takes 15 days, **C** finishes rest in 2 days, total pay = **₹ 2,400**.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time; Wage ∝ Work Done; Daily Wage = Efficiency × (Total Wage ÷ Total Work).

⇒ Work done by **A** and **B** in 5 days = 5 × (3 + 4) = 35 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 35 = 25 units.

⇒ Efficiency of **C** = 25 units ÷ 2 days = 12.5 units/day.

⇒ Wage per unit of work = 2400 ÷ 60 = ₹ 40.

⇒ Daily wage of **C** = Efficiency of **C** × Wage per unit = 12.5 × 40 = ₹ 500.

⇒ Daily wage of **A** = Efficiency of **A** × Wage per unit = 3 × 40 = ₹ 120.

⇒ Difference = 500 − 120 = ₹ 380.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages Principle

Wages are distributed in the ratio of total work done by each person. If people work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Daily Wage Formula

Daily Wage = Total Wage earned by a person ÷ Number of days worked by that person. Alternatively, Daily Wage = Efficiency (work per day) × Rate per unit of work.

Efficiency Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the task: Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.
